questions.q: When distressing things happen, what does the psalmist ask Yahweh not to do?
questions.a: When the psalmist calls out to Yahweh, he asks Yahweh to hear him and not to ignore him.

questions.q: To what does the psalmist compare the way he feels?
questions.a: The psalmist says he feels like grass that has withered.

questions.q: What has happened due to the psalmist’s distress?
questions.a: The psalmist is so miserable that he groans and his bones protrude under his skin.

questions.q: How do those who mock the psalmist use his name?
questions.a: Those who mock the psalmist use his name when they curse people.

questions.q: How does the psalmist say Yahweh has treated him in anger?
questions.a: The psalmist says it feels as if Yahweh has lifted him up and thrown him down.

questions.q: How long will Yahweh be remembered?
questions.a: The psalmist says that people of all times will talk about Yahweh.

questions.q: What do the servants of Yahweh cherish?
questions.a: Yahweh’s servants cherish even the stones and dust of Jerusalem.

questions.q: Why will the kings of the earth show respect for Yahweh?
questions.a: All the kings of the earth will recognize Yahweh’s glory.

questions.q: What does Yahweh do when the destitute pray?
questions.a: Yahweh listens to the prayers of the destitute and does not ignore them.

questions.q: How does the psalmist show how far into the future Yahweh’s praise will continue?
questions.a: He writes that people who are not even born yet will praise Yahweh.

questions.q: What did Yahweh see from heaven?
questions.a: From heaven Yahweh saw what was happening on the earth.

questions.q: For what purpose are the peoples and kingdoms gathered together?
questions.a: The peoples and kingdoms gather together to serve Yahweh.

questions.q: What does the psalmist plead with God not to do?
questions.a: The psalmist pleads with God not let him die too soon.

questions.q: What does the psalmist say Yahweh did in long ago?
questions.a: The psalmist says that long ago Yahweh made the earth and the heavens.

questions.q: Where does the psalmist say the descendants of Yahweh’s servants will live?
questions.a: The descendants of Yahweh’s servants will live in his presence.

commentary.text: A sorrowful complaint of great afflictions.
Encouragement by expecting the performances of God's promises to his church.

Verses 1–11 The whole word of God is of use to direct us in prayer; but here, is often elsewhere, the Holy Ghost has put words into our mouths. Here is a prayer put into the hands of the afflicted; let them present it to God. Even good men may be almost overwhelmed with afflictions. It is our duty and interest to pray; and it is comfort to an afflicted spirit to unburden itself, by a humble representation of its griefs. We must say, Blessed be the name of the Lord, who both gives and takes away. The psalmist looked upon himself as a dying man; My days are like a shadow.

We are dying creatures, but God is an everlasting God, the protector of his church; we may be confident that it will not be neglected. When we consider our own vileness, our darkness and deadness, and the manifold defects in our prayers, we have cause to fear that they will not be received in heaven; but we are here assured of the contrary, for we have an Advocate with the Father, and are under grace, not under the law. Redemption is the subject of praise in the Christian church; and that great work is described by the temporal deliverance and restoration of Israel. Look down upon us, Lord Jesus; and bring us into the glorious liberty of thy children, that we may bless and praise thy name.

Bodily distempers soon weaken our strength, then what can we expect but that our months should be cut off in the midst; and what should we do but provide accordingly? We must own God's hand in it; and must reconcile this to his love, for often those that have used their strength well, have it weakened; and those who, as we think, can very ill be spared, have their days shortened. It is very comfortable, in reference to all the changes and dangers of the church, to remember that Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, to-day, and for ever. And in reference to the death of our bodies, and the removal of friends, to remember that God is an everlasting God. Do not let us overlook the assurance this psalm contains of a happy end to all the believer's trials. Though all things are changing, dying, perishing, like a vesture folding up and hastening to decay, yet Jesus lives, and thus all is secure, for he hath said, Because I live ye shall live also.
